name: schema-violation-data-element-both-type-fields
description: A data element that states BOTH `application_type` and `implementation_type`. Since contract `8.0.0` a data element states the side of its type in exactly one of the two fields (`rule:interfaces.data_element.type-form`), and both names here are declared, each in its own layer — so what refuses is the shape of the payload, not a reference.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model plus the application type `SyntheticTorque`; the base's `implementation_types` layer declares `float32`. The change set creates an interface whose one data element names both.

authorization.notes: The scope covers every create exactly, so the answer is the engine's and not the authorization boundary's.

input.intent: Carry the synthetic torque on the bus.

value.name: ISyntheticTorque
value.description: The synthetic torque on the bus

expected.notes: Refused when the payload is bound, at the element the payload creates. The two legal repairs are the two fields: keep the one that names the side meant and drop the other. A data element that states neither is the other half of the same rule, `schema-violation-data-element-no-type-field`.
